observations: Flat density, no detours: 35 main-road boxes in groups of 1-6; all-box differs from clear only by the bonus (17%) and three slot crates.
Each idea appears once alone before it is combined: single, edge pair, sandwich, striped single, enemy, pond, mask, 2x2 block, checkpoint, timed crate.
Slot crates sit right after C1 and right before the goal - the two places players pause.
Both masks precede the next enemy cluster; pits are fatal regardless (F3 intro).
Every frog pond holds or borders a crate group: slowing water, enemy and reward share one spot.

Time crates (10 s) sit on block tops, stack tops, inside the 6-block and in the row: the trial tests vertical precision; walls give the fast line.

geometryObservations: **No mandatory jump on the main road.** Every hole is a notch from one edge or a pit in one half, the ponds can be waded, the trenches are planked and the bridges are walked (inferred from the map). Stage 1 teaches jumping with crates (the striped sandwich, the stack) and leaves gaps out.

**Lethal geometry lives at the edges.** Holes are cut from the road edge; the centre line is always safe. The risk comes from sweeping to an edge crate (S1-b, S1-g), and the intro states the rule plainly: a hole kills even with Aku.

**Water is the terrain variable.** Five or six ponds slow running but never kill; the first one spans the whole road before any lethal test. Water is shown harmless first, as Crash 2 does with mud (bible IX.4).

**Ponds are stations.** Each frog pond holds or borders a crate group (3-stack, 6-block, row of three), so slow ground, an enemy and a reward share one spot, and the frog is a projectile aimed at the crates.

**The walls are a second lane.** ≈1-high walls on both sides are runnable; the record line rides them past ponds and enemies and switches walls at holes. A skill route without a fork, with its own small snags (house doorway, hole edges).

**Every enemy keeps a territory.** Goats walk fixed straight lines, frogs stay in their ponds, knights stand at bridge entrances; nothing chases. The player decides when to engage, which suits a first stage.

**Knights guard chokes.** Both stand where the road narrows from ≈6–9 to ≈3–4 u between gate posts; the telegraph (the strain to lift, the tip stuck in the ground) gives a safe window, and the first knight is followed at once by a mask.
**Each enemy kind debuts alone.** Goat on wide flat road → frog alone in its pond → knight alone on a bridge → only then combinations (a goat between C1 and the slot crate, frogs as projectiles).

**Checkpoints on dry ground at a hazard exit.** C1 follows the big pond and the block, C2 the 6-block pond; but a hole waits a few steps past C1, so the calm respawn leads straight into the next decision.
**Plank crossings are the metronome.** Five full-width planks (1 + 2 + 1 in the main road + 1 after C2) punctuate the road at fairly even intervals, as visual beats with no risk.
**The bonus repeats the rule in side view:** the only falls are three tiny slab gaps at the start (the F3 hint says so), then flat walkways and a one-step drop to the crates.

**The time trial turns geometry into skill:** walls, holes and ponds become a wall-hopping line, and its hardest spot combines a frog projectile, a crate row on a raised ledge and an immediate jump onto the wall.
geometryTransfer: **Edge notches as the first lethal geometry.** On a 7–10 m (6–9 u) road, cut a `pit` 2.3–3.5 m into one edge and 2.3–3.5 m long, the next one 6–9 m further on the other edge; keep the centre line open. On foot nothing needs a jump; at board cruise the notches make a gentle carve. Put the first edge crate right beside the first notch.

**Walls as the skill lane.** Line the road with 1.15 m `wall`s on both sides (a full jump apex is 2.85 m; a grind jump 2.4 m): edges grind by default, so a skater rides the wall tops past slow ground and enemies. Break the wall at a notch so the line must switch sides, as the time-trial line does.

**Safe-failure water before lethal edges.** Without a slow-water surface, model a pond as a 0.5–0.8 m sunken dip in the road (terrain, no kill) that costs a jump to leave; put the first one across the full width before any lethal notch, and put a crate group and an enemy beside each later one.

**Gatekeeper at a bridge choke.** Narrow the road from 8–10 m to 3.5–4.5 m (3–4 u) between two posts and stand a telegraphed enemy there: a `charger` (0.70 s windup) or a `moa` (0.62 s wind-up, 0.9 s harmless recovery) plays the knight. Put a mask crate just past it, and repeat the choke once later with the level’s collectible behind it.

**Enemy beside crates as a projectile.** Patrol a `grunt` 2–3 m from a crate row; its carcass can be spun into the crates, the frog trick. Keep it on a short line so the player chooses when to engage.

**A hole a few metres past the checkpoint.** Place a 2.3 m wide notch in one half of the road 3–5 m past a checkpoint, with an enemy and a timed reward behind it, so the respawn is calm but the first move is a decision.
